findings.text: 适合AI生成代码后需要筛选死代码、未用导入和不可达组件的开发者。合格交付是经测试与人工核对的清理补丁，而不是告警清单本身。简单替代为终端graphlint query加人工复制结果；插件让Agent直接查图、重建索引和调整入口规则。不能根据告警自动删除框架回调或动态注册代码。

### Q04 · 最影响安全清理结论的是什么？ **研究主题**：缺陷与关键质疑 #### 完整回答 入口与动态调用建模决定死代码告警真假。上游明确静态分析无法证明getattr、反射等动态引用，因此告警不能直接变成删除授权。此外本组件优先使用PATH中的graphlint，未探测或绑定版本；固定插件源码不代表实际CLI就是该提交的算法，JSON可解析也不代表结论可靠。需要同时记录CLI版本和项目入口规则。 #### 证据与依据 **依据 1 · 作者声明**：[README.md:269-276](https://github.com/AngelosZou/graphlint/blob/4e810d8ff8a380d419316be91ec03936de37393b/README.md#L269-L276) 上游明确静态分析假阳性及入口配置边界。 ```text ## Limitations - **Static analysis only** — graphlint performs static analysis and cannot detect runtime linkage such as `getattr`, `importlib`, or dynamic dispatch patterns, which may result in false positives. This primarily affects Python; Rust's static dispatch model produces fewer false positives. **Mitigation:** add custom entry rules matching your codebase's conventions. For example, graphlint's own codebase uses `function_def:_detect_*` and `function_def:visit_*` patterns to prevent functions discovered via `getattr` from being flagged as dead. - **Python dynamic imports** — due to Python's dynamic import mechanisms (`importlib`, `getattr`, metaclasses, etc.), the default entry templates may produce false positives in codebases that rely heavily on runtime dispatch. Users should tune the `entry_rules` configuration to match their project's conventions. - **Rust macro expansion** — tree-sitter parses unexpanded source; procedural macros and `macro_rules!` bodies appear as opaque token trees. Some macro-generated call paths may be missed. `#[derive]` attributes are partially recognized via implicit `inherit` edges. - **C# partial classes & reflection** — tree-sitter parses each `.cs` file independently; partial class fragments are merged into a single logical node via `part_of` edges, but members called only through reflection (`Activator.CreateInstance`, DI container registration) may be missed, similar to Python's dynamic import limitations. - **C/C++ static analysis limits** — member calls resolve type-aware across translation units (via a project-wide class→method index), but there is **no virtual/overload/dynamic dispatch**: a call through a `Base*` pointer resolves statically to the base's method, so a derived override reached only that way may be reported dead. The preprocessor is treated as pure AST (`#if` is never evaluated, macros are not expanded); function-pointer indirect call targets are not traced; a `static` symbol in a header is per-TU. A pure-virtual (`= 0`) interface method is exempt from dead-code (dispatched by the vtable). - Node.js >= 20.
- A DeepSeek Harness profile (`dsh plugin` initializes one on first use).
- The graphlint CLI on `PATH` (`pip install graphlint`) or inside the project's

### Supported DSH core

The bundle imports `defineTool` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` at runtime — an
out-of-tree plugin resolves it from the running installation (it is one of the
plugin manager's protected modules) — and type-checks its tool definitions

| `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` | `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.3` |

Development and CI compile against the exact published versions pinned in

instead of failing a live tool call. Bump the pins with the core.

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `graphlint_query` | Query the dependency graph for dead code, unused imports, write-only variables, and other warnings. Fast incremental mode; JSON result. Common filters: `warn_types`, `graph_id`, `exclude_clean`, `include_tests`, `public_as_entry`. |
| `graphlint_build` | Full or incremental index rebuild as a **background job** (poll with `job_output`). |
| `graphlint_config` | `show` / `diff` / `get` / `set` entries in the project's `.graphlint/config.json`, plus `add-entry-rule` / `remove-entry-rule` / `add-exclude` / `remove-exclude` for custom entry rules and excludes. `diff` reports how the config differs from the shipped default rule template. |

The `graphlint` skill leads with these tools (they run inside the session working
directory and return structured results); the canonical CLI guidance follows as
reference.

### `root_dir` restriction

Every tool accepts an optional `root_dir`. It **must stay inside the session
working directory** (the default) — a hard guard rejects anything else with a
clear error. Scanning a high-level root (such as a user home directory) makes
graphlint build a huge first-time index and can block for many minutes.

The default root comes from the `workingDirectory` service (the seam that owns
a session's effective directory and repairs a deleted project), falling back to
the session header's original `cwd` and then to the harness process directory.
`graphlint_query` and `graphlint_config` then pass `--root-dir`; `graphlint_build`
and `graphlint config` run the CLI with that directory as their working
directory, because those subcommands read their own cwd.

### Optional Secondary working directories (`dsh-multi-folder`)

When the [dsh-multi-folder](https://github.com/AngelosZou/dsh-multi-folder)
plugin is installed and the user has configured secondary working directories
for the session, those directories automatically become valid `root_dir`
values for all three tools: the analysis root is accepted inside any configured
secondary directory, graphlint runs with that directory as its working
directory, and the index lands in its `.graphlint/`. A relative `root_dir`
still resolves against the primary session workspace.

This compatibility is automatic and optional. Each tool probes
`ctx.get('multiFolder')` at call time and nothing else changes:

- multi-folder absent, unconfigured, incompatible, or throwing → the plugin
  behaves exactly as if it did not exist (the guard falls back to the session
  working directory, and the refusal message keeps its original wording);
- multi-folder present → a refusal still names the configured secondary
  directories and the `/multi-folder` command that adds one, so the model
  learns the valid roots instead of retrying blindly.

The `multiFolder` service and the `workingDirectory` service are both optional
seams, read through `ctx.get` and never declared in `inject`, so neither plugin
becomes a hard dependency of the other.

[English](README.md) | [简体中文](docs/zh/README.md)

**Dead code detection for AI-generated codebases.**

AI agents generate code rapidly, leaving behind dead and redundant code that pollutes the LLM's context window and dilutes attention. Graphlint analyzes your codebase's dependency graph to identify entry points and **detect dead code** — components unreachable from any entry point — so agents can self-clean and keep the codebase lean.

## Supported Languages

| Language | Status | Parser | Features |
|----------|--------|--------|----------|
| **Python** (`.py`) | Built-in | `ast` (stdlib) | Decorators, type annotations, dynamic imports, framework-aware entry detection |
| **Rust** (`.rs`) | Built-in (opt-in deps) | `tree-sitter` | Attribute macros, traits, `pub` visibility, `macro_rules!` |
| **C#** (`.cs`) | Built-in (opt-in deps) | `tree-sitter` | Partial classes, properties/indexers/events, attributes, `.csproj` awareness, test framework entries |
| **C / C++** (`.c` `.h` `.cpp` `.cc` `.cxx` `.hpp` `.hh` `.hxx`) | Built-in (opt-in deps) | `tree-sitter` | struct/union/enum members, typedefs, macros, `#include` tracking, per-TU `static` linkage, C library entry mode, C++ classes/namespaces/templates, cross-TU member-call resolution |
| **TypeScript / JavaScript** (`.ts` `.tsx` `.js` `.jsx` `.mts` `.cts` `.mjs` `.cjs`) | Built-in (opt-in deps) | `tree-sitter` | JSX/React components, Next.js pages, NestJS decorators, Jest/Vitest tests, import/export analysis |
| **GDScript / Godot** (`.gd` `.tscn` `.tres` `project.godot`) | Built-in (opt-in deps) | `tree-sitter` + built-in resource parser | Scene/resource attachment, `preload`/`load`/`class_name`, main scene and autoload entries, editor-wired `[connection]` callbacks, `res://` path validation, dynamic-dispatch keep-alive |

Install optional language support:

```bash
pip install graphlint[rust]        # adds tree-sitter and tree-sitter-rust
pip install graphlint[csharp]      # adds tree-sitter and tree-sitter-c-sharp
pip install graphlint[c]           # adds tree-sitter + tree-sitter-c + tree-sitter-cpp (C/C++)
pip install graphlint[typescript]  # adds tree-sitter + tree-sitter-typescript + tree-sitter-javascript
pip install graphlint[godot]       # adds tree-sitter + tree-sitter-gdscript (.tscn/.tres/project.godot use the built-in parser)
```

> C/C++ are analysed by a **single unified C/C++ analyzer** that owns `.c .h .cpp
> .cc .cxx .hpp .hh .hxx`. It uses `tree-sitter-c` for C files, `tree-sitter-cpp`
> for C++ files, and routes a `.h` by the language of the TU(s) that include it
> — exactly as a C/C++ compiler does. One extra, `graphlint[c]`, installs both
> grammars.

> Godot is likewise analysed by a **single unified Godot analyzer** that owns
> `.gd` + `.tscn` + `.tres` + `project.godot`: scripts, scenes, resources and the
> project manifest must share one graph for `detect_entries()` to see the main
> scene, the autoloads, the script each scene attaches and the callbacks the
> editor wires in one pass. Scripts use `tree-sitter-gdscript`; the INI-like
> resource formats use a built-in parser.

## Features

- **Dead code detection** — finds components unreachable from any entry point via graph traversal
- **Multi-language support** — Python, Rust, C#, C/C++ (unified), TypeScript/JavaScript, and GDScript/Godot backends via a language adapter abstraction; Python uses stdlib `ast`, the others use `tree-sitter` (Godot's `.tscn`/`.tres`/`project.godot` use a built-in resource parser)
- **Language-specific awareness** — Python decorators, Rust attribute macros (`#[tokio::main]`, `#[test]`), C# attributes (`[Fact]`, `[HttpGet]`), C translation-unit scope (`static` internal linkage, per-TU header `static`s) and library entry mode, C++ classes/namespaces/templates, `enum class` members, and cross-TU member-call resolution, TS/JS JSX elements and ES module imports/exports, GDScript `class_name`/`signal`/`@export`/`@onready`/`@tool`/`@rpc`, scene and `ExtResource` attachment, trait implementations, `pub`/`public` visibility, partial classes, and more
- **AST/CST parsing** — extracts functions, methods, structs, enums, traits, impls, macros, classes, properties, indexers, events, variables, and fields; aware of type annotations, destructured variables, and generics
- **Dependency graph** — builds directed edges: `read`, `write`, `call`, `inherit`, `decorate`
- **Entry point detection** — built-in rules covering Python frameworks (FastAPI, Flask, Django, Click, Typer, Celery, pytest), Rust conventions (main, async runtimes, WASM, proc macros, FFI, tests, pub API), .NET conventions (console, xUnit, NUnit, MSTest, Web API, Minimal API, Generic Host, WinForms, WPF), C/C++ conventions (`main`/`WinMain`/`wWinMain`/`DllMain`/`_tmain` for C and a free `main` for C++, `class_definition:` patterns, `test_file` by convention, and C library mode via external-linkage symbols), TS/JS conventions (main, module index, CLI/server listen, Next.js pages, NestJS decorators, React JSX, Jest/Vitest tests), and Godot conventions (the `project.godot` manifest, `class_name` public classes, `@tool` editor scripts, `@rpc` remote methods, GUT/gdUnit4 tests, literal string dispatch and `.tscn`-wired callbacks) plus custom rules
- **Configurable entry templates** — add custom entry rules via `ast_pattern` prefixes including `function_call:`, `function_def:`, `decorator:`, `class_definition:` (C#), `file_match:`, `file_is_program` (C#), `visibility:pub` (Rust), `visibility:public` (C#), `trait_impl:` (Rust), `macro_def:` (Rust), `jsx_element:` (TypeScript), `export:` (TypeScript), and more
- **`--public-as-entry` flag** — treat all public items (Rust `pub`, C# `public`, C external-linkage symbols) as entry points for library analysis
- **Warning detection** — 10 warning types including unused imports, write-only variables, dead code, and more
- **Incremental updates** — after initial full scan, only changed files are re-indexed; delta-aware reachability analysis avoids full-graph recomputation; incompatible index schema versions are auto-detected and rebuilt
- **Python API + CLI** — integrate into any Tool, CI pipeline, or let agents self-analyze and self-clean

## Quick Start

### Agent Integration

Graphlint installs its usage guidance into your AI coding tools at the **global level**:

```bash
# Install the graphlint skill (~/.agents/skills/graphlint/SKILL.md) — default, recommended
graphlint install
graphlint install --targets all      # also ~/.claude/skills/graphlint/SKILL.md

# Install the DeepSeek Harness plugin (recommended in DSH — tool-based integration)
graphlint install dsh --profile web

# Inject the prompt into agent config files (opencode, cursor, codex, cc)
graphlint install prompt

# Copy the prompt to clipboard for manual paste into your agent
graphlint prompt

# Remove installed skills / prompts
graphlint uninstall
```

All channels derive from one canonical skill document shipped in the package (`graphlint/skill.md`), so the skill file, the injected prompt and the DeepSeek Harness plugin's `graphlint` skill can never drift apart. For details, see [Agent Integration](docs/en/guide/agent-integration.md). For tools you'd like native support for, feel free to submit an [issue](https://github.com/AngelosZou/graphlint/issues) — these requests are typically handled quickly.

### DeepSeek Harness Plugin

A plugin bundle for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin ecosystem ships in this repository under [integrations/dsh](integrations/dsh/):

- **Tools** — `graphlint_query` (dependency-graph queries with structured results), `graphlint_build` (index build as a background job, polled with `job_output`), `graphlint_config` (show/diff/get/set for `.graphlint/config.json`).
- **Skill** — a `graphlint` skill teaches the agent when and how to use the tools.
- **Safety** — tools default to the session working directory and hard-refuse any root outside it, so an accidental high-level scan cannot block a turn.

Install the bundle from npm:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-graphlint
```

Then restart `dsh web`. To link a local checkout instead (development):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/AngelosZou/graphlint.git
cd graphlint/integrations/dsh
npm install
npm run build

# 2. Link the bundle into a profile (run from the repository root)
cd ..
dsh plugin --profile web add link:./integrations/dsh

# 3. Restart dsh web
```

### CLI

```bash
# Find dead code in current directory
graphlint query --warn-types "dead_code"

# Full analysis with JSON output
graphlint query --json

# View a specific graph detail
graphlint query -g 1 --detail full

# Exit non-zero when dead code or unused imports found (for CI)
graphlint query --json --fail-on dead_code,unused_import

# Treat all public items as entry points (library analysis mode)
graphlint query --public-as-entry

# Rebuild index
graphlint build --force

# Configure
```

### Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` | Success — no warnings matched `--fail-on` |
| `1` | Error — invalid parameters, exception, or config error |
| `2` | Warnings found — `--fail-on` matched specified warning types |

Use `--fail-on` with a comma-separated list of warning types to make `graphlint query` return exit code `2` when matching warnings are found. This enables CI pipeline integration without blocking on non-critical warnings.

Graphlint is static-analysis based and cannot recognize certain Python dynamic references (e.g., `getattr`, `importlib`), which may produce unexpected exit codes. Only use `--fail-on` for CI blocking behavior when you're confident in your configuration. Agents are better suited for logic that requires contextual judgment. See [Limitations](#limitations) for details.

### Python API

```python
from graphlint.api import query

# Find dead code components
result = query(warn_types="dead_code", json_output=True)

# Full dependency graph analysis
result = query(include_tests=True, json_output=True)
```

## Limitations

- **Static analysis only** — graphlint performs static analysis and cannot detect runtime linkage such as `getattr`, `importlib`, or dynamic dispatch patterns, which may result in false positives. This primarily affects Python; Rust's static dispatch model produces fewer false positives. **Mitigation:** add custom entry rules matching your codebase's conventions. For example, graphlint's own codebase uses `function_def:_detect_*` and `function_def:visit_*` patterns to prevent functions discovered via `getattr` from being flagged as dead.
- **Python dynamic imports** — due to Python's dynamic import mechanisms (`importlib`, `getattr`, metaclasses, etc.), the default entry templates may produce false positives in codebases that rely heavily on runtime dispatch. Users should tune the `entry_rules` configuration to match their project's conventions.
- **Rust macro expansion** — tree-sitter parses unexpanded source; procedural macros and `macro_rules!` bodies appear as opaque token trees. Some macro-generated call paths may be missed. `#[derive]` attributes are partially recognized via implicit `inherit` edges.
- **C# partial classes & reflection** — tree-sitter parses each `.cs` file independently; partial class fragments are merged into a single logical node via `part_of` edges, but members called only through reflection (`Activator.CreateInstance`, DI container registration) may be missed, similar to Python's dynamic import limitations.
- **C/C++ static analysis limits** — member calls resolve type-aware across translation units (via a project-wide class→method index), but there is **no virtual/overload/dynamic dispatch**: a call through a `Base*` pointer resolves statically to the base's method, so a derived override reached only that way may be reported dead. The preprocessor is treated as pure AST (`#if` is never evaluated, macros are not expanded); function-pointer indirect call targets are not traced; a `static` symbol in a header is per-TU. A pure-virtual (`= 0`) interface method is exempt from dead-code (dispatched by the vtable). C function parameters are not modelled as nodes, so a parameter named like a caller's local can resolve by flat name.
- **`--public-as-entry` scope** — this flag applies to languages with `public` visibility declarations (Rust `pub`, C# `public`). It has no effect on Python files. Toggling this flag triggers a full re-index. For long-term library analysis, prefer enabling the `rust_pub_api` entry rule via `graphlint config` to persist the setting.
- **Godot dynamic dispatch** — string dispatch (`call("name")`, `emit_signal("x")`, `set("prop")`), `load(variable)`, `get_node(variable)`, `Expression.parse`, Callables stored in containers, and GDExtension/plugin entry points cannot be proven statically. By default (`godot.method_dead_code: false`) only file/asset-level verdicts are produced (orphan script, unreachable scene, unused `.tres`); per-method verdicts are opt-in. Literal dispatch names and `.tscn`-wired callbacks act as entries, a script containing anything unprovable keeps all its members alive (`godot.assume_dynamic_keeps_file_alive`) and receives a `dynamic_import` advisory. Godot 4.x syntax only.
- **Large codebase build time** — on a large codebase with 700+ `.py` files, 1,000+ classes, and 14,000+ functions, a full rebuild takes approximately 200 seconds (actual performance depends on hardware). Small projects (~60 files) complete in ~1 second. This cost is one-time, after the initial full scan, subsequent queries use incremental updates.

import { buildArgv } from '../args.js'
import { resolveGraphlint } from '../python.js'
import { SECONDARY_ROOT_NOTE, guardAllowedRoot, resolveSessionCwd } from '../root.js'

const ROOT_DESCRIPTION =
  'Project root directory to build the index for. Defaults to the session working directory. ' +
  'Only pass the working directory itself or one of its subdirectories — building an index for a high-level root ' +
  '(such as a user home directory) can take many minutes. ' +
  SECONDARY_ROOT_NOTE

const OUTPUT_LIMIT_BYTES = 64_000

/**
 * The live runtime Agent's session id, which is what `ctx.jobs.start({ owner })`
 * takes.
 *
 * `@deepseek-ai/dsh-jobs` declares `owner?: SessionId` (a STRING) and its local
 * implementation resolves it through the agent registry
 * (`agents.get(session)`). Passing the Agent object instead — which this tool
 * used to do — resolves to `undefined` and makes the registry throw
 * `session "[object Object]" has no live agent`, AFTER the CLI process was
 * already spawned. The published `Agent` face types exactly `{ id }`, so the
 * read is typed and safe.
 */
function sessionIdOf(exec: ToolRunContext): string | undefined {
  const agent = exec.agent as { id?: unknown } | undefined
  return typeof agent?.id === 'string' && agent.id.length > 0 ? agent.id : undefined
}

export function registerBuildTool(ctx: PluginContext): void {
  ctx.tools.register(
    defineTool({
      name: 'graphlint_build',
      description:
        'Build or rebuild the graphlint index as a background job; poll it with job_output using the returned job id. ' +
        'Runs `graphlint build` with the project root as its working directory. ' +
        ROOT_DESCRIPTION,
      parameters: {
        root_dir: { type: 'string', description: ROOT_DESCRIPTION },
        force: { type: 'boolean', description: 'Force a full index rebuild (default: incremental).' },
      },
      output: {
        schema: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: true },
        render(_args, value) {
          const v = value as { error?: string; job_id?: string } | null
          if (v && typeof v.error === 'string') return [{ type: 'text', text: `[graphlint] error: ${v.error}` }]
          const id = v && typeof v.job_id === 'string' ? v.job_id : 'unknown'
          return [
            {
              type: 'text',
              text: `[graphlint] build started as background job ${id}. Poll with job_output; a first-time full build can take minutes.`,
            },
          ]
        },
      },
      timeoutMs: 15_000,
      async execute(args, exec: ToolRunContext): Promise<Record<string, JsonValue>> {
        const sessionRoot = await resolveSessionCwd(exec, ctx.get?.bind(ctx))
        const extraRoots = await secondaryDirs(ctx, sessionRoot)
        let rootDir: string
        try {
          rootDir = guardAllowedRoot(args.root_dir, sessionRoot, extraRoots)
        } catch (err) {
          return { error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) }
        }
        const exe = await resolveGraphlint(ctx.subprocess, ctx.fs, rootDir)
        if (!exe) return { error: 'graphlint CLI not found. Install with: pip install graphlint' }
        const handle = ctx.subprocess.spawn({
          argv: buildArgv(exe, args.force === true),
          cwd: rootDir,
          stdio: {
            stdin: 'ignore',
            stdout: { maxBytes: 1_048_576 },
            stderr: { maxBytes: 262_144 },
          },
          graceMs: 15_000,
          signal: exec.signal,
          env: { PYTHONIOENCODING: 'utf-8' },
        })
        let jobId: string
        try {
          jobId = ctx.jobs.start({
            kind: 'graphlint-build',
            label: `graphlint build${args.force === true ? ' --force' : ''} in ${rootDir}`,
            outputLimitBytes: OUTPUT_LIMIT_BYTES,
            owner: sessionIdOf(exec),
            run: () => {
              let stdoutCursor = 0
              let stderrCursor = 0
              return {
                cancel: () => handle.terminate(),
                done: handle.done.then(
                  (outcome) =>
                    outcome.exitCode === 0
                      ? { status: 'completed' as const, detail: 'index build finished' }
                      : outcome.exitCode === null
                        ? { status: 'killed' as const, detail: 'process tree terminated' }
                        : { status: 'failed' as const, detail: `exit code: ${outcome.exitCode}` },
                  (err) => ({
                    status: 'failed' as const,
                    detail: String((err as { message?: string })?.message ?? err),
                  }),
                ),
                readOutput: () => {
                  const parts: string[] = []
                  const stdoutReader = handle.collected?.stdout
                  if (stdoutReader) {
                    const read = stdoutReader.readFrom(stdoutCursor)
                    stdoutCursor = read.nextOffset
                    if (read.text.length > 0) parts.push(read.text)
                  }
                  const stderrReader = handle.collected?.stderr
                  if (stderrReader) {
                    const read = stderrReader.readFrom(stderrCursor)
                    stderrCursor = read.nextOffset
                    if (read.text.length > 0) parts.push(read.text)
                  }
                  return parts.join('')
                },
              }
            },
          })
        } catch (err) {
          // `jobs.start` preflights ownership and the per-owner job limit and may
          // throw AFTER the child was spawned. Without this the build process
          // would be left running with no job able to collect or stop it.
          handle.terminate()
          return { error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) }
        }
        return { job_id: jobId }
      },
    }),
  )
}

import type { AgentLike, WorkingDirectoryService } from './types.js'

/**
 * What {@link sessionCwd} and {@link resolveSessionCwd} read from one tool
 * execution. Structural on purpose: it is satisfied by the engine's
 * `ToolRunContext` and by the plain objects the unit tests build, so the
 * functions stay testable without importing the whole execution type.
 */
export interface SessionContext {
  readonly agent?: AgentLike | undefined
  readonly signal?: AbortSignal | undefined
}

/**
 * Absolute working directory the executing session was created in.
 *
 * This is the DSH framework keyword for the session workspace; it is NOT the
 * same as the deployment-wide sandbox workspace root. Falling back to
 * `process.cwd()` keeps the value defined even for executors that omit the
 * agent chain.
 *
 * This is the SYNCHRONOUS fallback. Prefer {@link resolveSessionCwd}, which
 * asks the supported `workingDirectory` seam first; this one reads the live
 * Agent's session header directly (the augmented runtime shape) and exists for
 * the path where no working-directory service is mounted.
 */
export function sessionCwd(exec: SessionContext | undefined): string {
  const header = exec?.agent?.session?.header
  if (header && typeof header.cwd === 'string' && header.cwd.length > 0) return header.cwd
  return process.cwd()
}

/**
 * Resolve the analysis root for one tool call.
 *
 * Order: the `workingDirectory` service (the seam that owns the session's
 * effective directory and can repair a deleted project), then the session
 * header's original cwd, then the process directory.
 *
 * The service is read through `ctx.get` rather than declared in `inject`, so a
 * deployment without it keeps working. `ensure()` runs against the live runtime
 * Agent (`exec.agent`), which the published `Agent` face describes as `{ id }`
 * alone; the value is forwarded unchanged and the seam sees the real
 * augmented object.
 */
export async function resolveSessionCwd(
  exec: SessionContext | undefined,
  lookup?: (name: string) => unknown,
): Promise<string> {
  const agent = exec?.agent
  if (agent !== undefined && lookup !== undefined) {
    const service = lookup('workingDirectory') as WorkingDirectoryService | undefined
    if (service && typeof service.ensure === 'function') {
      try {
        const directory = await service.ensure(agent, exec?.signal)
        if (typeof directory === 'string' && directory.length > 0) return directory
      } catch {
        // The seam refused (no live agent, deleted project, cancellation). Fall
        // back to the header/process directory rather than failing the call:
        // the root guard still bounds whatever we return.
      }
    }
  }
  return sessionCwd(exec)
}

/**
 * Model-facing sentence naming the extra roots a tool call may also target.
 * Shared by the tool descriptions so the three tools say the same thing.
 */
export const SECONDARY_ROOT_NOTE =
  "A root inside one of the session's secondary working directories (dsh-multi-folder) is accepted as well."

/** Raised when a requested analysis root escapes every allowed root. */
export class RootOutsideSessionError extends Error {
  constructor(
    public readonly requested: string,
    public readonly sessionRoot: string,
    public readonly extraRoots: readonly string[] = [],
  ) {
    const configured =
      extraRoots.length === 0
        ? ''
        : " or inside one of the session's secondary working directories (" + extraRoots.join(', ') + ')'
    const remedy =
      extraRoots.length === 0
        ? ''
        : " Add the directory with the user's /multi-folder command to make it a valid analysis root."
    super(
      `root_dir must stay inside the session working directory (${sessionRoot})${configured}; got ${requested}. ` +
        'Scanning a high-level root (e.g. a user home directory) builds a huge index and can block for many minutes.' +
        remedy,
    )
    this.name = 'RootOutsideSessionError'
  }
}

/** True when `root` equals `base` or lies inside it (case-insensitive on Windows). */
export function isWithin(base: string, root: string): boolean {
  const rel = relative(base, root)
  if (rel === '') return true
  const normalized = process.platform === 'win32' ? rel.toLowerCase() : rel
  return normalized !== '..' && !normalized.startsWith('..' + sep) && !isAbsolute(normalized)
}

/**
 * Resolve the requested analysis root and refuse anything outside the session
 * working directory.
 *
 * graphlint indexes every source file under its root; letting a tool call
 * point at a high-level directory (home dir, drive root) turns a fast
 * incremental query into a multi-minute first-time index build. The guard
 * fails fast with a clear message instead of blocking the turn.
 */
export function guardRoot(requested: string | undefined, sessionRoot: string): string {
  return guardAllowedRoot(requested, sessionRoot, [])
}

/**
 * Multi-root guard: the primary workspace plus optional extra roots (the
 * dsh-multi-folder secondary working directories, when that plugin is
 * configured for this session). Relative paths resolve against the primary
 * workspace; an absolute target is accepted when it lands inside ANY allowed
 * root. With no extra roots this is exactly {@link guardRoot}.
 *
 * An extra root is a directory the USER granted the session through
 * `/multi-folder`, so it is trusted exactly like the primary workspace: the
 * guard's purpose is to keep the model from pointing graphlint at an
 * unintended drive-wide root, not to second-guess a configured grant.
 */
export function guardAllowedRoot(
  requested: string | undefined,
  sessionRoot: string,
  extraRoots: readonly string[] = [],
): string {
  const primary = resolve(sessionRoot)
  const wanted = requested !== undefined && requested.trim().length > 0 ? requested : primary
  const root = resolve(primary, wanted)
  if (isWithin(primary, root)) return root
  for (const extra of extraRoots) {
    if (isWithin(resolve(extra), root)) return root
  }
  throw new RootOutsideSessionError(root, primary, extraRoots)
}

/** The subprocess seam as this plugin consumes it. */
type Subprocess = PluginContext['subprocess']

export interface RunLimits {
  /** Upper bound for waiting on process exit before terminating the tree. */
  doneCapMs: number
  /** Grace period the subprocess service uses between SIGTERM and SIGKILL. */
  graceMs: number
}

export const DEFAULT_LIMITS: RunLimits = { doneCapMs: 120_000, graceMs: 15_000 }

export interface RunOutcome {
  exitCode: number | null
  stdout: string
  stderr: string
  /** True when the done cap fired and the process tree was terminated. */
  timedOut: boolean
}

function withTimeout<T>(timer: TimerService, promise: Promise<T>, ms: number): Promise<T | 'timeout'> {
  return new Promise((resolvePromise) => {
    const cancel = timer.timeout(() => resolvePromise('timeout'), ms)
    promise.then(
      (value) => {
        cancel()
        resolvePromise(value)
      },
      () => {
        cancel()
        resolvePromise('timeout')
      },
    )
  })
}

function readAll(reader: { readFrom(offset: number): { text: string } } | undefined): string {
  if (!reader) return ''
  return reader.readFrom(0).text
}

/**
 * Spawn a graphlint CLI invocation with collected stdio and await its exit.
 *
 * Hardening rules learned from the first prototype:
 * - force UTF-8 (`PYTHONIOENCODING`) so localized code pages cannot garble output;
 * - wire the caller's AbortSignal so the cooperative tool timeout can terminate the tree;
 * - cap the exit wait so a wedged build cannot hang the tool turn;
 * - never shell-interpret argv.
 */
export async function runGraphlint(
  subprocess: Subprocess,
  timer: TimerService,

import type { PluginContext } from './types.js'

/** The subprocess and filesystem seams as this plugin consumes them. */
type Subprocess = PluginContext['subprocess']
type Fs = NonNullable<PluginContext['fs']>

const WINDOWS_BINS = [
  'env\\Scripts\\graphlint.exe',
  '.venv\\Scripts\\graphlint.exe',
  'venv\\Scripts\\graphlint.exe',
]

const POSIX_BINS = ['env/bin/graphlint', '.venv/bin/graphlint', 'venv/bin/graphlint']

/**
 * Locate a runnable graphlint CLI.
 *
 * Resolution order: the `graphlint` console script on PATH, then the common
 * project-local virtualenv script locations under the analysis root. Returns
 * null when graphlint is not installed anywhere reachable.
 */
export async function resolveGraphlint(
  subprocess: Subprocess,
  fs: Fs | undefined,
  rootDir: string,
): Promise<string | null> {
  try {
    const exe = await subprocess.resolveExecutable('graphlint')
    if (exe) return exe
  } catch {
    /* PATH lookup failed; fall through to virtualenv probes */
  }
  const bins = process.platform === 'win32' ? WINDOWS_BINS : POSIX_BINS
  for (const rel of bins) {
    const candidate = join(rootDir, rel)
    try {
      const target = await fs?.resolve(candidate, { cwd: rootDir })
      if (target === undefined) continue
      const info = await fs?.stat(target)
      if (info) return candidate
    } catch {
      /* probe failed */
    }
  }
  return null
}

import type { JsonValue } from './types.js'

export type GraphSummaryLike = {
  graph_id: number
  entry: string
  warnings?: JsonValue[]
  is_dead_code?: boolean
}

/** One node of a single-graph detail payload (`query --graph-id <id> --json`). */
export type GraphDetailNode = {
  node_id?: number
  name?: string
  qualified_name?: string
  node_type?: string
  file_path?: string
  line_start?: number
  line_end?: number
  is_deprecated?: boolean
  type_annotation?: string | null
  decorators?: JsonValue[]
}

/** One edge of a single-graph detail payload. */
export type GraphDetailEdge = {
  source_name?: string
  target_name?: string
  edge_type?: string
  file_path?: string
  line?: number
}

/** One warning of a single-graph detail payload. */
export type GraphDetailWarning = {
  warn_type?: string
  severity?: string
  message?: string
  file_path?: string
  line?: number
}

/**
 * The payload of `query --graph-id <id> --json`.
 *
 * Detail mode is a DIFFERENT envelope from the list query, not a variant of it:
 * the CLI (`graphlint/query/formatter.py::format_json_detail`) emits it under
 * the top-level `graph` key with no `result.graphs` at all. A parser that only
 * knows the list shape therefore rejects every detail query, however healthy
 * the CLI is. Nodes/edges/files are capped by the CLI (30/10/10) and the
 * `*_omitted` counters report how many entries that cap cut.
 */
export type GraphDetail = {
  graph_id: number
  entry?: string
  files?: string[]
  nodes?: GraphDetailNode[]
  edges?: GraphDetailEdge[]
  warnings?: GraphDetailWarning[]
  edges_omitted?: number
  nodes_omitted?: number
  files_omitted?: number
}

export type QueryFailure = {
  ok: false
  error: string
  exitCode: number | null
  stdoutTail?: string
  stderrTail?: string
}

export type QuerySuccess = {
  ok: true
  exitCode: number | null
  queryTimeMs?: number
  result: {
    graphs: GraphSummaryLike[]
    total_graphs?: number
    has_more?: boolean
    warnings_summary?: Record<string, number>
  }
  /** `[graphlint]`-prefixed notice lines the CLI wrote to stderr even on success
   *  (e.g. the one-time default-rule-template update notice). */
  stderrNotes?: string[]
  rootDir?: string
}

/** A successful `query --graph-id <id>` run — the single-graph envelope. */
export type QueryDetailSuccess = {
  ok: true
  exitCode: number | null
  queryTimeMs?: number
  graph: GraphDetail
  stderrNotes?: string[]
  rootDir?: string
}

export type QueryOutcome = QueryFailure | QuerySuccess | QueryDetailSuccess

/** The two success shapes `renderQueryText` can render. */
export type QueryTextOutcome = QuerySuccess | QueryDetailSuccess

const TAIL_LENGTH = 500

/** Caps for the model-facing detail text — the CLI's own cap is 30/10/10. */
const DETAIL_LIMITS = { warnings: 10, nodes: 15, edges: 10, files: 5 }

/** `[graphlint]`-prefixed notice lines from stderr, even when the query succeeded. */
function stderrNotices(stderr: string): string[] {
  return stderr
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter((line) => line.startsWith('[graphlint]'))
}

/** True when a success outcome carries a single-graph detail payload. */
export function isDetailOutcome(outcome: QueryTextOutcome): outcome is QueryDetailSuccess {
  return 'graph' in outcome
}

export function parseQueryOutput(stdout: string, stderr: string, exitCode: number | null): QueryOutcome {
  if (stdout.trim().length === 0) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      error: `graphlint produced no output (exit ${exitCode})`,
      exitCode,
      stderrTail: stderr.slice(-800),
    }
  }
  let parsed: unknown
  try {
    parsed = JSON.parse(stdout)
  } catch {
    return {
      ok: false,
      error: `could not parse graphlint JSON output (exit ${exitCode})`,
      exitCode,
      stdoutTail: stdout.slice(-TAIL_LENGTH),
      stderrTail: stderr.slice(-TAIL_LENGTH),
    }
  }
  const record = parsed as {
    result?: unknown
    graph?: unknown
    status?: unknown
    message?: unknown
    query_time_ms?: unknown
    root_dir?: unknown
  }
  // The CLI reports a semantic failure (e.g. `Graph #999 not found`) as an
  // error envelope on an exit-0 run, so this must be checked BEFORE the success
  // shapes: otherwise the real reason is swallowed as an unknown shape.
  if (record.status === 'error') {
    const message =
      typeof record.message === 'string' && record.message.trim().length > 0
        ? record.message
        : 'graphlint reported an error'
    return {
      ok: false,
      error: message,
      exitCode,
      ...(stderr.trim().length > 0 ? { stderrTail: stderr.slice(-TAIL_LENGTH) } : {}),
    }
  }
  const queryTimeMs = typeof record.query_time_ms === 'number' ? record.query_time_ms : undefined
  const rootDir = typeof record.root_dir === 'string' ? record.root_dir : undefined
  // Detail envelope (`--graph-id`): a single `graph` object, no `result.graphs`.
  const detail = record.graph
  if (
    typeof detail === 'object' &&
    detail !== null &&
    typeof (detail as { graph_id?: unknown }).graph_id === 'number'
  ) {
    const notices = stderrNotices(stderr)
    return {
      ok: true,
      exitCode,
      ...(queryTimeMs !== undefined ? { queryTimeMs } : {}),
      graph: detail as GraphDetail,
      ...(notices.length > 0 ? { stderrNotes: notices } : {}),
      ...(rootDir !== undefined ? { rootDir } : {}),
    }
  }
  // List envelope: `result.graphs`.
  const result = record.result
  if (typeof result !== 'object' || result === null || !Array.isArray((result as { graphs?: unknown }).graphs)) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      error: `unexpected graphlint JSON shape (exit ${exitCode})`,
      exitCode,
      stdoutTail: stdout.slice(-TAIL_LENGTH),
    }
  }
  const notices = stderrNotices(stderr)
  return {
    ok: true,
    exitCode,
    queryTimeMs,
    result: result as QuerySuccess['result'],
    ...(notices.length > 0 ? { stderrNotes: notices } : {}),
    rootDir,
  }
}

/** One-line description of a failure outcome, for render blocks. */
export function failureText(outcome: QueryFailure): string {
  const tail = outcome.stderrTail ?? outcome.stdoutTail
  return tail ? `[graphlint] error: ${outcome.error}\n${tail}` : `[graphlint] error: ${outcome.error}`
}

function hasWarnings(g: GraphSummaryLike): g is GraphSummaryLike & { warnings: JsonValue[] } {
  return Array.isArray(g.warnings) && g.warnings.length > 0
}

/** Model-facing summary lines for a successful query — list or detail mode. */
export function renderQueryText(outcome: QueryTextOutcome): string[] {
  return isDetailOutcome(outcome) ? renderGraphDetailText(outcome) : renderListText(outcome)
}

/** Model-facing summary lines for a list query. */
function renderListText(outcome: QuerySuccess): string[] {
  const r = outcome.result
  const lines: string[] = []
  const shown = r.graphs.length
  const total = r.total_graphs ?? shown
  lines.push(
    `[graphlint] query ok — ${total} component(s), ${shown} shown` +
      (r.has_more ? ' (more available)' : '') +
      (outcome.queryTimeMs !== undefined ? `, ${outcome.queryTimeMs}ms` : ''),
  )
  const dead = r.graphs.filter((g) => g.is_dead_code === true).length
  if (dead > 0) lines.push(`dead-code components: ${dead}`)
  const summary = r.warnings_summary
  if (summary && typeof summary === 'object') {
    const parts = Object.entries(summary).map(([key, value]) => `${key}:${value}`)
    if (parts.length > 0) lines.push(`warnings: ${parts.join(', ')}`)
  }
  const interesting = r.graphs.filter(hasWarnings).slice(0, 10)
  for (const g of interesting) {
    lines.push(`  #${g.graph_id} ${g.entry} [${g.warnings.length} warning(s)]`)
  }
  for (const note of outcome.stderrNotes ?? []) lines.push(note)
  return lines
}

/** ` pkg/mod.py:12-14` — the location suffix of a detail entry, when it has one. */
function location(filePath: string | undefined, line: number | undefined, end?: number | null): string {
  if (typeof filePath !== 'string' || filePath.length === 0) {
    return typeof line === 'number' ? `:${line}` : ''
  }
  if (typeof line !== 'number') return ` ${filePath}`
  return typeof end === 'number' && end !== line ? ` ${filePath}:${line}-${end}` : ` ${filePath}:${line}`
}

/** Model-facing lines for a single-graph detail query. */
function renderGraphDetailText(outcome: QueryDetailSuccess): string[] {
  const g = outcome.graph
  const files = g.files ?? []
  const nodes = g.nodes ?? []
  const edges = g.edges ?? []
  const warnings = g.warnings ?? []
  const lines: string[] = []
  const entry = typeof g.entry === 'string' && g.entry.length > 0 ? g.entry : '(no entry point — unreachable component)'
  lines.push(
    `[graphlint] graph #${g.graph_id} detail — entry: ${entry}` +
      (outcome.queryTimeMs !== undefined ? `, ${outcome.queryTimeMs}ms` : ''),
  )
  const omitted: string[] = []
  if ((g.nodes_omitted ?? 0) > 0) omitted.push(`${g.nodes_omitted} node(s)`)
  if ((g.edges_omitted ?? 0) > 0) omitted.push(`${g.edges_omitted} edge(s)`)
  if ((g.files_omitted ?? 0) > 0) omitted.push(`${g.files_omitted} file(s)`)
  lines.push(
    `files: ${files.length}, nodes: ${nodes.length}, edges: ${edges.length}, warnings: ${warnings.length}` +
      (omitted.length > 0 ? ` (+ ${omitted.join(', ')} omitted by the CLI's display cap)` : ''),
  )
  if (warnings.length > 0) {
    lines.push(`warnings (${warnings.length}):`)
    for (const w of warnings.slice(0, DETAIL_LIMITS.warnings)) {
      const kind = w.warn_type ?? 'warning'
      const severity = typeof w.severity === 'string' && w.severity.length > 0 ? ` [${w.severity}]` : ''
      const message = typeof w.message === 'string' && w.message.length > 0 ? ` — ${w.message}` : ''
      lines.push(`  ${kind}${severity}${location(w.file_path, w.line)}${message}`)
    }
    if (warnings.length > DETAIL_LIMITS.warnings) {
      lines.push(`  … ${warnings.length - DETAIL_LIMITS.warnings} more warning(s)`)
    }
  }
  if (nodes.length > 0) {
    lines.push(`nodes (${nodes.length}):`)
    for (const n of nodes.slice(0, DETAIL_LIMITS.nodes)) {
      const name = n.name ?? '(unnamed)'
      const type = typeof n.node_type === 'string' && n.node_type.length > 0 ? ` (${n.node_type})` : ''
      const deprecated = n.is_deprecated === true ? ' [deprecated]' : ''
      const id = typeof n.node_id === 'number' ? `#${n.node_id} ` : ''
      lines.push(`  ${id}${name}${type}${location(n.file_path, n.line_start, n.line_end)}${deprecated}`)
    }
    if (nodes.length > DETAIL_LIMITS.nodes) {
      lines.push(`  … ${nodes.length - DETAIL_LIMITS.nodes} more node(s)`)
    }
  }
  if (edges.length > 0) {
    lines.push(`edges (${edges.length}):`)
    for (const e of edges.slice(0, DETAIL_LIMITS.edges)) {
      const src = e.source_name ?? '?'
      const dst = e.target_name ?? '?'
      const type = typeof e.edge_type === 'string' && e.edge_type.length > 0 ? ` (${e.edge_type})` : ''
      lines.push(`  ${src} -> ${dst}${type}${location(e.file_path, e.line)}`)
    }
    if (edges.length > DETAIL_LIMITS.edges) {
      lines.push(`  … ${edges.length - DETAIL_LIMITS.edges} more edge(s)`)
    }
  }
  if (files.length > 0) {
    lines.push(`files (${files.length}):`)
    for (const f of files.slice(0, DETAIL_LIMITS.files)) lines.push(`  ${f}`)
    if (files.length > DETAIL_LIMITS.files) {
      lines.push(`  … ${files.length - DETAIL_LIMITS.files} more file(s)`)
    }
  }
  for (const note of outcome.stderrNotes ?? []) lines.push(note)
  return lines
}
